theme: Superior-mirage inversion becomes a two-level trickster whose apparent face is displaced above its real body.

evolution_design.regional_evidence: WMO describes superior mirages over cold surfaces with warmer air above, sometimes lifting or inverting distant images. NPS documents cold water and fog on Lake Superior; the local creature placement is an inference from suitable lake conditions, not a sourced specific sighting.
evolution_design.original_invention: The fake hovering face is an original solid body lobe supported by a narrow bent neck; no transparency, gradient or rendering trick is required for the sprite.

body_growth.body: A low dark mask-shaped body stands on two short feet; an inverted pale false-face flap rises just above it on a short S-neck. Real eyes peek from the lower rim.
body_growth.silhouette: Two stacked unequal masks connected by a visible short bent neck.

body_growth.body: The false-face flap expands into a broad inverted crown above a small low body. Two folded side vanes open like flat horizon bars; the real lower eyes remain visible beneath a broad collar. Its broad horizon vanes carry the real body on rising shore winds beneath the displaced false face.
body_growth.silhouette: Wide high inverted crown over a very low narrow body, with two horizon-bar side vanes; no ghost wisps.

silhouette_concept: Two stacked unequal masks connected by a visible short bent neck. → Wide high inverted crown over a very low narrow body, with two horizon-bar side vanes; no ghost wisps.
habitat: Cold lake lookouts and sheltered shore ledges during inversion-like weather.

proposed_routes.placement: Lake-facing lookout above the pebble/basalt district; no new mirage visual-effect system assumed.
proposed_routes.status: encounter proposal only; no map or story mutation

sources.title: WMO International Cloud Atlas, Mirage
sources.supports: Cold-surface superior mirage, inversion and apparent image displacement.

sources.supports: Regional Lake Superior cold-water weather and fog; this source is a Wisconsin park, not a Minnesota sighting.

nonduplication: Unlike auroraF013 and sundogF069, the design uses an inverted false horizon and two solid stacked body lobes, without glowing curtains, sun halos or decoy-hound anatomy.
sprite_constraints: Native56x56 front full body facing left;48x48 close rear portrait facing upper-right. Four colors per species, individually planned after design lock. Large solid anatomical landmarks, stepped black exterior anchors, sparse internal marks; no gradients, particles or texture-dependent identity.
